{{Short description|On mathematics of sums of prime powers}}
The '''Waring–Goldbach problem''' is a problem in [[additive number theory]], concerning the representation of [[integer]]s as sums of powers of [[prime number]]s. It is named as a combination of [[Waring's problem]] on sums of powers of integers, and the [[Goldbach conjecture]] on sums of primes. It was initiated by [[Hua Luogeng]]<ref>L. K. Hua: [http://qjmath.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/pdf_extract/os-9/1/68 Some results in additive prime number theory], ''Quart. J. Math. Oxford'', '''9'''(1938), 68&ndash;80.</ref> in 1938.

==Problem statement==
It asks whether large numbers can be expressed as a sum, with at most a constant number of terms, of like powers of primes. That is, for any given positive integer ''<math>k</math>'', is it true that all sufficiently large numbers can be written as <math>(p_1)^k+(p_2)^k+\cdots+(p_t)^k</math>, where <math>p_1,p_2,...,p_t</math> are primes and ''<math>t</math>'' is at most some constant value?<ref>{{cite journal|last=Buttcane|first=Jack |date=January 2010|title=A note on the Waring–Goldbach problem|journal=Journal of Number Theory|publisher=Elsevier|volume=130|issue=1|pages=116–127|doi=10.1016/j.jnt.2009.07.006|doi-access=}}</ref>

The case <math>k=1</math> is a weak version of the Goldbach conjecture. Some progress has been made for ''<math>k \leqslant 7</math>.''

==Heuristic justification==
By the [[prime number theorem]], the number of ''<math>k</math>''<sup>th</sup> powers of a prime below ''<math>X</math>'' is of the order ''<math>\frac{\sqrt[k]{X}}{\log X}</math>''. From this, heuristically, the number of sums of ''<math>t</math>'' terms which are at most ''<math>X</math>'' is roughly ''<math>\left(\frac{\sqrt[k]{X}}{\log X}\right)^t</math>.'' It is reasonable to assume that for some sufficiently large number ''<math>t</math>'' this is ''<math>X-c</math>'', i.e., all numbers up to ''<math>X</math>'' are ''<math>t</math>''-fold sums of ''<math>k</math>''<sup>th</sup> powers of primes. This argument is, of course, a long way from a strict proof.

==Relevant results==
{{Expand section|Published results that are very similar, or that are likely to contribute to its eventual proof|date=March 2010}}

In his monograph,<ref>Hua Lo Keng: ''Additive theory of prime numbers'', Translations of Mathematical Monographs, '''13''', American Mathematical Society, Providence, R.I.  1965 xiii+190 pp</ref> using and refining the methods of [[Hardy–Littlewood circle method|Hardy, Littlewood]] and [[Ivan Matveyevich Vinogradov|Vinogradov]], Hua Luogeng obtained ''<math>O(k^2\log k)</math>'' upper bound for the number of terms required to exhibit all sufficiently large numbers as the sum of <math>k</math><sup>th</sup> powers of primes.

Every sufficiently large odd integer is the sum of 21 fifth powers of primes.<ref>{{citation|first1=Koichi|last1=Kawada|first2=Trevor D.|last2=Wooley|title=On the Waring–Goldbach problem for fourth and fifth powers|journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]]|year=2001|volume=83|issue=1|pages=1–50|doi=10.1112/plms/83.1.1|hdl=2027.42/135164|url=https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/2027.42/135164/1/plms0001.pdf|hdl-access=free}}.</ref>
